recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future editorial cleanup of the awkward streaming bullet can be handled separately, but no semantic source fix is needed for FHIR-16902.
issue_request: FHIR-16902 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked for clarification on whether Binary retrieval may support byte ranges, pre-read size discovery using HEAD, streaming, dynamically generated content, or live-stream-like content; the resolution was to add a note that servers may support these features if they want.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 9686e4489dce88c02db1f229de8bc1d4782c5a4c, corresponding to svn revision 14352 from the Jira comment. That commit added source/binary/binary-notes.xml Read prose listing byte ranges, size discovery, streaming, and dynamic generation, followed by the statement that servers are free but not required to support them.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes binary=Binary, so the Binary resource narrative is in current build scope. Later related Binary HEAD wording work, including FHIR-18340, refined the same note and is already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-19254 was a later no-change issue about external validation/tool behavior rather than a source-text change. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision for Binary advanced-read support.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/binary/binary-notes.xml:89-104 already says the specification makes no rules for advanced read functionality such as byte ranges, content size checks with HEAD, streaming, and dynamic generation, and that servers are free but not required to support these features.
